section.title: Newton's method
section.p: Linear approximation estimates a function by a line.
Newton's method uses that line to solve an equation.

The solution is a point where the graph of f crosses the x-axis. If we already have a nearby guess x_0, the tangent line at x_0 is often easier to use than the curve itself. The tangent line crosses the x-axis at a new guess.

subsection.title: Convergence when the starting point is good
subsection.p: Newton's method can be fast. But it is not magic. It is a local method, just like linear approximation.
The method works best when:

li.p: the starting guess is close to the root,
the function is smooth near the root,
the derivative at the root is not zero.

subsection.p: The third condition means the graph crosses the axis with a real slope, not with a flat touch.

This is why Newton's method can suddenly become very accurate. If an error is about 10^{-3}, its square is 10^{-6}. If an error is about 10^{-6}, its square is 10^{-12}.
This behavior is called quadratic convergence.

note.title: The reason Newton can be fast
note.p: Near a simple root, Newton's method does not merely reduce the error. It roughly squares the error.

subsection.title: Failure modes: cycles and bad tangents
subsection.p: Newton's method depends on tangent lines. A bad tangent can send the method to the wrong place, make it cycle, or stop it entirely.
The hypotheses are not decoration.

paragraphs.title: Failure mode 1: a horizontal tangent
paragraphs.p: then the tangent line is horizontal. It does not cross the x-axis in the way the method needs.
The Newton formula cannot even produce x_1. The function has roots, but this starting point gives a horizontal tangent.

paragraphs.title: Failure mode 2: a cycle
paragraphs.p: But the function does have a real root. Since
the Intermediate Value Theorem tells us that there is a root between -2 and -1.
Newton's method failed because the tangent lines from 0 and 1 point back to each other.

figure.caption: For f(x)=x^3-2x+2, Newton's method starting at 0 cycles between 0 and 1.

paragraphs.title: Failure mode 3: a multiple root
paragraphs.p: then Newton's method may still converge, but often more slowly.
This moves halfway toward 1 each time. It converges, but the error is cut in half rather than squared. The fast convergence is lost.

subsection.title: How to use Newton's method safely
subsection.p: Newton's method is most reliable when it is used with a picture or with a bracket.
A practical workflow is:

li.p: Graph f, or use signs to locate an interval where a root should lie.
Choose a starting point near the root.
Stop only when both x_n has stabilized and f(x_n) is small.
If the method behaves strangely, try a different starting point or use bisection.

subsection.p: The bisection method is slower, but if f is continuous and changes sign on an interval, bisection is dependable. Newton's method is faster when it behaves well.

note.title: Newton's method in one sentence
note.p: Replace the curve by its tangent line, solve the linear problem, and repeat.

subsection.p: Linear approximation has now done two jobs. It estimated how errors move through a formula, and it solved equations by tangent-line correction.

The next models take one more step. Sometimes the rule we know is not a formula for y, but a formula for y'. Growth, decay, cooling, and population change are often written first as laws about derivatives.
